questions.prompt: What is the second reading?
questions.hint: Where does R start counting?
questions.ok: R counts positions from 1, so bp[2] is the second reading, 140.

questions.prompt: Summarise the week's readings
questions.hint: You want one typical value for the week.
questions.ok: mean() adds the four readings (554) and divides by 4: 138.5.

questions.prompt: Which readings get flagged?
questions.hint: A comparison on a vector checks every item.
questions.ok: The comparison runs on every reading: 140 and 151 are 140 or above, so visits 2 and 4 are TRUE.

questions.prompt: The nurse's script counts 1 flag. Which line?
questions.hint: Read the clinic rule again: "140 or above".
questions.ok: > leaves out exactly 140, so visit 2 is missed. The rule says 140 or above, which is >=: 2 flags.

questions.prompt: Which visits need a follow-up?
questions.hint: You want positions, not a count.
questions.ok: which() gives the positions where the comparison is TRUE: visits 2 and 4.

questions.prompt: What is the pulse pressure?
questions.hint: Systolic minus diastolic.
questions.ok: Pulse pressure is the systolic minus the diastolic: 120 - 80 = 40.

questions.prompt: Work out the mean arterial pressure
questions.hint: MAP is the diastolic plus a third of the pulse pressure.

questions.prompt: What does round(map) print?
questions.hint: round() with no second number gives a whole number.
questions.ok: round(93.33333) goes to the nearest whole number: 93.

questions.prompt: The doctor's formula gives 40. Which line?
questions.hint: Look at what the brackets wrap.
questions.ok: The brackets wrap everything, so dbp cancels out: 120 / 3 = 40. Only the pulse pressure should be divided.

questions.prompt: Write the line for the notes
questions.hint: paste() joins pieces with spaces.
questions.ok: paste() joins "MAP:", 93 and "mmHg" with spaces: "MAP: 93 mmHg".

questions.prompt: What does the wristband ID print?
questions.hint: toupper() changes the letters only.
questions.ok: toupper() turns the letters into capitals; digits and the dash stay the same.

questions.prompt: How many characters is the ID?
questions.hint: Count characters inside the text.
questions.ok: nchar() counts the characters: s, -, 0, 0, 4, 2 is 6.

questions.prompt: What does the full wristband label print?
questions.hint: paste0() adds nothing between pieces.
questions.ok: paste0() joins with no space, and toupper() runs first: "WARD7-S-0042".

questions.prompt: The number part comes out as "-004". Which line?
questions.hint: Count the positions of each character.
questions.ok: Positions 2 to 5 are "-004". The digits sit at positions 3 to 6: substr(id, 3, 6).

questions.prompt: What is the next ID number?
questions.hint: Turn the text into a number before adding.
questions.ok: as.numeric("0042") is 42, and 42 + 1 is 43.

questions.prompt: How many readings are in the log?
questions.hint: length() counts items.
questions.ok: length() counts the items in the vector: 4 readings.

questions.prompt: Show the lowest and highest together
questions.hint: One function gives two numbers back.
questions.ok: range() returns the smallest and largest values: 5.4 and 11.2.

questions.prompt: What is the average reading?
questions.hint: mean() adds and divides by the count.
questions.ok: 30.4 / 4 = 7.6 mmol/L on average.

questions.prompt: The script counts 0 problem readings. Which line?
questions.hint: Can one reading be both high and low?
questions.ok: & needs both TRUE at once, which never happens. | means either: sum(high | low) is 1.

questions.prompt: Which readings were high?
questions.hint: Put the condition inside the square brackets.
questions.ok: gluc[gluc > 10] keeps the readings where the condition is TRUE: 11.2.

code: for (n in cases) total = total + n

questions.prompt: What total does R print?
questions.hint: n takes each day's count in turn.
questions.ok: The loop adds every day: 3 + 5 + 9 + 14 = 31 cases.

questions.prompt: Build the running total for the chart
questions.hint: Each round should add one value to the end.
questions.ok: c(running, total) adds the new total to the end each day: 3, 8, 17, 31.

questions.prompt: How much did cases rise each day?
questions.hint: Both sides are vectors of three days.
questions.ok: R subtracts the two vectors item by item: 5 - 3, 9 - 5, 14 - 9 = 2, 4, 5.

questions.prompt: The officer's total is 17. Which line?
questions.hint: Count how many days the loop visits.
questions.ok: 1:3 stops at day 3, so day 4's 14 cases are missed. seq_along(cases) covers every day.

questions.prompt: How many times higher is the last day than the first?
questions.hint: Compare the largest day with the smallest.
questions.ok: 14 / 3 = 4.666667: cases rose about 4.7-fold in four days.
